data.cultural_impact: The name Hanumantha holds immense significance in Indian culture, and it is synonymous with bravery, courage, and unwavering devotion. Lord Hanuman, who is depicted as a monkey god, is known for his superhuman abilities, and the name Hanumantha is a reminder of these qualities. Hanuman is a central figure in the Hindu epic Ramayana, and his actions and devotion to Lord Rama and his sensus place him as an embodiment of ideal devotion and a symbol of liberation from suffering.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hanumantha is also deeply spiritual, symbolizing the power of devotion and the importance of staying loyal and true to one's chosen path or deity. The Hanuman Chalisa, abhakti poem composed in the Awadhi language, emphasizes Hanuman's qualities of devotion, courage, and selflessness. Reciting the Hanuman Chalisa is believed to bring happiness, prosperity, and protection from all troubles. The spiritual significance of the name Hanumantha reminds us of the importance of staying devoted to our chosen path and deity, and remaining steadfast in our beliefs and actions, despite any challenges or obstacles we may face.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Hanumantha represents strength, devotion, and selflessness. The 'tha' symbol in his name signifies purity and detachment, emphasizing his unwavering loyalty to Lord Rama. Hanuman's embodiment of bravery and unwavering faith underscores the power of devotion in overcoming difficulties.

historical_references.reference: Hanuman is considered an incarnation of Shiva and is revered as the god of strength and courage. He is the central character in the Indian epic Ramayana and is known for his unwavering devotion to Lord Rama.
historical_references.context: The Ramayana is an ancient Indian epic that narrates the life of Prince Rama and his adventures. Hanuman is a key figure in this narrative who helps Rama in his quest to rescue his wife Sita from the demon king Ravana.

historical_references.reference: Hanuman is also believed to have been born in Treta Yuga, an epoch in Hindu cosmology, as the son of Anjani and the wind god Vayu. He is said to have acquired his immense strength by consuming the powerful herb Sanjeevani Parvata from the mountain Gandhamadana, at the request of Lord Rama, to save his brother Lakshmana from death.
historical_references.context: Treta Yuga is one of the four ages in Hindu cosmology. Hanuman's birth and his role in the Ramayana provide vivid examples of his strength, devotion, and unwavering loyalty.

modern_usage.modern_context: Hanumantha, also known as Hanuman, is a central figure in Hindu mythology and is revered as a god of strength, courage, and loyalty. He is depicted as an ardent devotee of Lord Rama and is known for his unwavering devotion and selflessness. In modern contexts, Hanumantha is seen in various forms across different platforms. In Hindu temples, he is worshipped as a deity and his idols are installed in temples worldwide. In Hindi cinema, Hanumantha is a popular character and is often portrayed as a hero and a symbol of strength and bravery. In literature and poetry, Hanumantha is a recurring character and is celebrated for his devotion and courage. The trend of Hanumantha's popularity continues to grow, reflecting the enduring significance of Hindu mythology and devotionalism in contemporary society.
